task: Execute the reverse-engineering drill on Palladium Fantasy 1e combat, character progression, and subsystem integration.
delivery: current canonical drill plus guided analysis
observations: Active defense creates meaningful defensive agency but adds a resolution step to applicable incoming attacks, so its execution cost scales with attack count and participant count.
The rules use several unrelated resolution families across combat, skills, attributes, saves, recovery, and other subsystems; learning one procedure does not reliably teach the next.
A missing formal rule can be deliberate delegation to player or referee judgment rather than an accidental mechanical hole.
notes: The drill produced architectural observations without reducing the analysis to a preference judgment.

task: Compare Rifts Ultimate Edition against its older Palladium chassis using the reverse-engineering drill and inspect how later mechanics integrate with inherited rules.
delivery: current canonical drill plus guided comparison
observations: Adding new domains without refactoring the core produced conversion rules, stacking exceptions, parallel damage scales, and situational patches that increased completeness faster than coherence.
A rule can remain executable while accumulating adapter logic that signals architectural mismatch between subsystems.
Legacy preservation can make the game serve an inherited mechanic rather than reevaluating whether that mechanic still expresses the expanded design requirements.
notes: The same analysis vocabulary used on Palladium Fantasy transferred to a later edition and exposed accretion rather than merely greater rule volume.

task: Compare Star Frontiers and FrontierSpace as examples of detailed science-fiction RPG design, focusing on reusable primitives, action economy, adjudication, and subsystem reuse.
delivery: current canonical drill plus cross-system comparison
observations: Detailed rules remained easier to reason about when many situations reused the same probability grammar or action-check operation instead of introducing new resolution families.
FrontierSpace's multi-action penalty concentrates several tactical tradeoffs into one reusable rule, so added complexity directly creates decisions about present action versus later defense.
Explicitly allowing adjudication through existing abilities and skills limits rule growth when an edge case can already be expressed by the system's mechanical vocabulary.
Mechanical detail was allocated according to play importance, as shown by simplified minor NPCs and scalable detail rather than fully specifying every entity.
notes: The drill transferred from critique of failure modes to recognition of healthy crunch and constructive architecture.

task: Compare Knight Hawks starship construction with FrontierSpace vehicle and starship design to test whether extensive configuration creates meaningful build differentiation.
delivery: current canonical drill plus construction-system stress test
observations: Knight Hawks offers substantial construction procedure while hull-size dependencies cause many same-class ships to converge on similar mechanical identities.
A construction system can expose many configuration choices while still having a narrow practical possibility space when parent variables pre-determine most downstream behavior.
Separating size from independently adjustable performance and capability parameters increases conceptual breadth without requiring every concept to ignore balance constraints.
notes: The comparison produced a repeatable stress test: attempt several different intended roles within one broad class and check whether the rules pull them toward the same final build.

task: Compare Star Frontiers Alpha Dawn with Zebulon’s Guide as an established-system extension case, using the reverse-engineering drill to separate additive expansion from replacement architecture and migration cost.
delivery: current canonical drill plus guided comparative review
observations: Alpha Dawn’s direct percentile grammar remained recognizable across abilities, skills, and combat, while Zebulon replaced a high-frequency learned dependency with a resolution table, column shifts, result colors, and result shifts even though much of the surrounding combat sequence remained familiar.

Zebulon added substantial high-value content—new character concepts, races, Frontier relationships, equipment, body computers, security technology, and optional mental powers—whose play value was largely separable from the replacement resolution architecture.

Character conversion exposed several kinds of compatibility beyond numeric translation: capability coverage, relative power, role philosophy, and play identity could change even when old characters were technically convertible.

Optional mental powers were comparatively well isolated because removing the module left the defined base game operational, showing that radical additive content can be less disruptive than a core dependency replacement.
notes: The comparison converted a historical edition/supplement dispute into reusable tests for dependency depth, migration, optionality, capability granularity, and additive versus replacement change without treating newer design as automatically better.

task: Review historical noncanonical Star Frontiers redesign, expanded-skill, and robot-construction prototypes alongside direct retrospective playtest evidence to test complexity placement and mixed-revision diagnosis.
delivery: current canonical playtest AP and mechanics Patterns applied to practitioner artifacts plus human-taught test history
observations: A historical redesign replaced trained skill checks with target-number d10 dice pools and success counting while retaining percentile ability checks; the playtest group stopped after one session and requested a return to the original core rules.
The same group liked the expanded skill options, so rejection of the redesigned package did not establish that every changed component had failed.

A separate unfinished robot-construction subsystem introduced substantial optional complexity in mission, bodies, programs, power, sensors, armor, and equipment, yet the group welcomed it because the complexity created new capabilities and construction decisions instead of taxing every familiar action.
The mixed result supports decomposing bundled revisions into retained, rejected, and unresolved components and treating reversion to a known-working baseline as a legitimate outcome.
notes: The artifacts are practitioner evidence, not Star Frontiers canon. Their value is the contrast between a rejected high-frequency resolution replacement and welcomed additive skill/construction complexity under the same game and table context.

delivery: current canonical drill plus source-grounded review and practitioner feedback
notes: The review qualified earlier complexity lessons by separating decision complexity from operator complexity, adding concurrent-state cost and curation burden, and distinguishing good runtime defaults from persistent dependency accounting. Practitioner experience is evidence about usability outcome, not a claim that all audiences should reject high-detail play.
observations: GURPS repeatedly reused a coherent small mechanical vocabulary across tasks, combat, hazards, vehicles, magic, and powers, but the same shared state also allowed individually conditional rules to become simultaneously active and propagate through common resources such as HP, FP, Move, Dodge, and derived values.

An interested player who enjoyed major parts of the system and played several sessions declined to GM it because the volume of optional detail created a curation barrier: knowing what could be omitted safely appeared to require broad system mastery before a first campaign.

Skill-to-skill defaults were useful as runtime competency transfer but became high-maintenance when purchased advancement had to be reinterpreted against changing derived baselines; correct mathematics did not eliminate the risk of an incorrect persistent character sheet when dependencies were forgotten.

Combat and magic contained substantial complexity that more often earned its cost by creating visible tactical, resource, mastery, and character-expression decisions, while much of the broader simulation burden consisted of lookup, arithmetic, state maintenance, and concurrent bookkeeping.

The same simulation depth was judged much more attractive in a computer implementation because software could maintain dependency graphs, timers, modifiers, and status cascades while leaving the player-facing decisions intact, provided the causes of automated results remained inspectable.

Fourth Edition psionics reused Advantages, modifiers, and source-specific counters instead of creating a second full power engine, while magic used a bespoke spell structure where ritual, mana, energy, prerequisites, and mastery produced a distinct desired play experience.
task: Review GURPS Fourth Edition Basic Set as a standalone core-system teardown, including character architecture, skills, advancement, combat, injury, hazards, vehicles, magic, psionics, onboarding, and human-operating burden.

Compare GURPS Third Edition, Third Edition Revised, Compendium-era extensions, and Fourth Edition to identify preserved play identity, promoted subsystem innovations, removed legacy dependencies, unresolved burdens, and character-economy changes.
delivery: current canonical edition-comparison drill plus source-grounded comparative review and practitioner feedback
observations: Fourth Edition preserved the recognizable one-second maneuver combat and point-built character identity while making architectural changes such as repricing DX, moving HP to ST and FP to HT, decomposing secondary characteristics, removing Passive Defense, and regularizing active-defense formulas.

Late Third Edition supplements and Compendia acted as laboratories for later core grammar: Enhancements and Limitations escaped superhero and psionic origins, Maneuvers generalized into Techniques, and optional ST/HT-derived rules foreshadowed Fourth Edition defaults.

Generalization sometimes made older duplicate infrastructure removable: Fourth Edition rebuilt psionics on Advantages, modifiers, Talents, and source-specific counters rather than retaining the separate Third Edition Power-plus-Skill engine, while magic remained bespoke because its spell-learning and ritual structure still produced a distinct desired experience.

Third Edition Revised explicitly removed an introductory adventure to make room for accumulated generic rules, strengthening reference completeness for established users while illustrating how mature-system consolidation can displace novice-facing executable onboarding.

Fourth Edition substantially improved the skill grammar and promoted one-way parent Techniques, yet retained reciprocal skill-default advancement rebaselining, showing that a single legacy dependency can survive a broad refactor and continue to dominate manual bookkeeping burden.

Character economics improved when Fourth Edition priced broad attributes by leverage, provided independently purchasable secondary characteristics and intermediate Talents, and parameterized behavioral-disadvantage severity; however, allowing disadvantages to finance positive abilities still preserved incentive pressure to fill the permitted negative-point budget.

Firearm and damage refactoring moved stable distinctions such as penetration and piercing size into reusable attack data, while removal of Passive Defense deleted several downstream exceptions that had accumulated around the older abstraction.

Fourth Edition generalized late-Third-Edition racial packages into editable character templates, reusable lenses, meta-traits, and explicit composition rules, providing progressive disclosure over the point-buy catalog without turning role templates into hard permission boundaries.

Social architecture became more orthogonal in Fourth Edition: Rank, privilege, wealth, reputation, relationships, language proficiency, and cultural familiarity were separated into distinct state, while coarse language proficiency replaced a more dependency-heavy numeric language-skill model where adjacent levels often mattered less than broad competence categories.

Advancement economics became more internally consistent when Fourth Edition removed the older double-cost surcharge for raising attributes after character creation and clarified that points price persistent character state while fictional permission and cause determine whether a change can occur; however, detailed study and causal tracking can become facilitator surveillance if enforced at unnecessary resolution.

Templates exposed a product-level asymmetry: GURPS successfully encoded curation for novice character creation but did not generalize the same preset-and-lens idea as strongly to novice GM rules configuration, where optional-rule selection still depended heavily on expert knowledge.

Whole-lineage comparison showed that Fourth Edition was a substantial architectural refactor rather than a clean-sheet replacement: it improved internal regularity and generalized successful supplement mechanics while deliberately preserving the simulation-heavy point-build and one-second tactical play identity.

Genre supplements functioned as design laboratories: mechanics proven in focused domains could escape into shared grammar and later eliminate duplicate subsystem infrastructure, supporting a supplement-to-core refactoring cycle rather than treating every extension as permanent local machinery.

Architectural cleanup did not necessarily reposition the experience: Fourth Edition combat, damage, and character construction became cleaner and more orthogonal without becoming a light RPG, so implementation quality and pacing/operating profile must be evaluated separately.

Mature-edition consolidation served veteran reference needs differently from novice facilitator needs; stronger canonical coverage and indexing did not by themselves supply a known-good first-campaign configuration, safe omissions, or progressive expansion triggers.

GURPS remained strong evidence that detailed simulation is not inherently poor design: the main unresolved costs were manual operating burden, novice curation burden, reciprocal skill-default maintenance, and selected point-economy incentives rather than simulation itself.
notes: The comparison treats 4E as an evolutionary refactor of installed GURPS rather than a clean-sheet system. Practitioner experience anchors migration and usability effects; source text anchors documented rule changes. Final synthesis separates architectural improvement from experiential repositioning, veteran reference value from novice onboarding, and simulation depth from manual operator burden; it does not treat detailed simulation, large rulesets, or newer editions as inherently good or bad.

task: Compare Rolemaster Standard System and Rolemaster Fantasy Role Playing as successive core-system generations, tracing character architecture, action economy, maneuvers, combat, injury, magic, advancement, information architecture, and table-level operating burden.
delivery: current canonical reverse-engineering drill plus source-grounded edition comparison and practitioner evidence
observations: Rolemaster tables frequently compressed real logic: attack tables combined weapon family, armor interaction, damage, and critical severity, while critical and maneuver tables generated contextual consequences rather than merely restating arithmetic.

The aggregate workflow remained expensive because common-path actions chained classification, modifier gathering, roll, lookup, branch, secondary lookup, state generation, and later state maintenance; shared d100 did not imply one operational resolution grammar.

The percentage activity and OB/DB allocation systems created meaningful timing and offense-versus-defense choices, but one-percent granularity and repeated modifier translation added operator work beyond the decision resolution required.

Rolemaster SS compounded runtime cost with cross-book dependency: core combat and spell procedures pointed to Arms Law or Spell Law for required tables, so expert table-location memory functioned as a learned interface cache that novices did not possess.

Rolemaster FRP materially improved core executability and retrieval locality by consolidating many specialized weapon and maneuver tables into shared family structures plus compact differentiating data, localizing required critical/fumble/spell-failure tables, and curating the option catalog without substantially changing Rolemaster’s simulation identity.

FRP therefore behaved as a major usability and information-architecture refactor rather than a major common-path complexity refactor: percentage activity, parry allocation, multi-stage attacks, persistent wound states, detailed casting conditions, granular XP accounting, and long recovery times largely remained.

One practitioner report from a four-player-plus-GM SS session described completing the first action in a combat round and being able to leave the table for about ten minutes without missing the next turn, supporting serial-round-latency as a usability dimension while remaining anecdotal rather than a universal timing measure.

Severe injury and spell-failure outcomes could impose recovery measured in weeks or months, showing that fictional consequence duration must be evaluated against campaign cadence and return to meaningful player participation rather than only medical or simulation plausibility.
The user enjoyed reading Rolemaster’s tables while loathing the burden of operating the system, demonstrating that reference-content entertainment and runtime usability are independent qualities.
notes: The comparison grants Rolemaster a clean trial rather than treating table use or simulation depth as inherently bad. Source text supports procedure and edition-architecture claims; practitioner evidence supports one observed usability outcome. The synthesis distinguishes local table compression from global workflow cost, expert reference architecture from novice retrieval, and interface refactoring from experiential repositioning.

delivery: current canonical drill plus guided lineage comparison
notes: The lineage comparison supplied both a positive complexity case (resource scarcity with compressed contents) and a negative minimalism case (missing starship construction), sharpening the distinction between rules quantity and decision value.
observations: BareBones Fantasy achieves much of its compactness through categorical compression and shared resolution grammar rather than merely omitting procedures.

FrontierSpace expands the d00Lite engine primarily by recombining broad inputs, progressively disclosing character complexity, and reusing the same resolution sentence across character, vehicle, and starship domains.
FrontierSpace resource tracking preserves scarcity as a decision engine while aggregating low-value medical, technical, energy, fuel, and life-support detail into low-friction trackable units.

Complexity cost depends strongly on cadence: high-frequency common-path procedure is expensive, while infrequent downtime or construction procedure can be worthwhile when it creates durable strategic or expressive decisions.

Stock examples and upgrade rules do not fully replace a construction grammar when a campaign-central ownership domain is expected to support user-authored instances, as illustrated by FrontierSpace starships.
task: Review BareBones Fantasy and FrontierSpace as a d00Lite lineage case, focusing on scope expansion, resource abstraction, complexity cadence, GM delegation, and starship support.

delivery: current canonical reverse-engineering drill plus source-grounded edition comparison and practitioner evidence
notes: The case separates simulation detail from operator burden and compares editions by preserved behavior, relocated complexity, and persistent decision value rather than treating modernization or a different die system as inherently superior.
observations: Twilight: 2000 showed that detailed logistics can create high-value play when food, fuel, fatigue, maintenance, medicine, cargo, personnel, and route choice compete through shared bottlenecks such as time, labor, capacity, mobility, and future risk.

1E Coolness Under Fire modeled continuous combat stress by limiting adaptive decision throughput while allowing simple precommitted behavior and leadership-assisted cognitive offloading, preserving player agency more effectively than a generic competence penalty.

Version 2.2 vehicle damage preserved component-specific persistent failure states while replacing 1E internal projectile-path tracing with categorical penetration-margin results, demonstrating that output granularity and causal-resolution granularity can be separated.

Version 2.2 automatic fire exposed a high-frequency scaling problem in which operator work can grow with burst or projectile count faster than meaningful decision count, so nominal specialist complexity must be budgeted by actual genre frequency.

Both editions repeatedly allocated more mechanical state to persistent PCs, vehicles, wounds, contacts, and campaign assets than to disposable NPCs or provisional entities, supporting progressive simulation by expected persistence.
The user prefers 1E over Version 2.2 overall despite acknowledging genuine 2.2 improvements, especially because 1E retained stronger continuous stress behavior through Coolness Under Fire.
task: Review Twilight: 2000 1E and Version 2.2 as standalone systems, compare the edition delta, and extract reusable game-design lessons about simulation, resource coupling, combat stress, cadence, persistent state, and procedural compression.

delivery: current canonical reverse-engineering drill plus source-grounded subsystem analysis
notes: The case avoids equating age or crunch with poor design. It distinguishes internal subsystem quality from table-wide participation, generic resolver structure from genre-specific surrounding state, and scenario support from campaign automation. Source-specific findings such as REF dominance, Humanity as cybernetic alienation, and Netrunning isolation remain bounded to the reviewed ruleset.
observations: Cyberpunk 2020 used a shallow STAT + Skill + 1D10 common grammar while genre specificity emerged from Roles, persistent state, equipment access, cyberware, Reputation, medical consequences, institutions, and dependencies around that grammar.

Roles were best understood as privileged world interfaces whose value depended on cadence, consequence, exclusivity, participation coverage, and campaign ecology rather than raw numerical equivalence.

Lifepath generated unresolved scenario-addressable state: enemies, friends, relationships, debts, injuries, institutional threats, and motives could survive character creation as future campaign pressure.

REF demonstrated dependency-density and first-strike amplification: initiative, attack competence, broad skill coverage, reflex enhancement, full-auto margin, and wound feedback compounded its value without proving that high-value attributes are universally broken.

Friday Night Firefight kept the attempt/miss path cheap and expanded detailed state after successful hits; hit location routed protection and limb consequences while a global wound track compressed overall injury state.
Automatic fire compressed projectile generation but could still multiply expensive per-hit consequence processing, showing that cadence multiplication can break a good low-frequency mechanic.
Cyberware, financing, drugs, medicine, and institutional services repeatedly linked capability to persistent dependency, vulnerability, access, maintenance, or reduced autonomy.

Stabilization, treatment, recovery, replacement, and Trauma Team made the aftermath of violence part of campaign time and economy; long character recovery still had to be checked against player-level TBMD.

Netrunning had strong internal specialist decision output but poor mixed-party participation coverage because exclusive verbs, separate state, and one-second Net timing could concentrate many human decision cycles in one player while others watched.

Night City, corporate profiles, reusable NPCs, Never Fade Away, and Screamsheets provided strong scenario machinery, especially when shared problems exposed multiple professional solution interfaces; dynamic campaign evolution remained largely Referee synthesis.
task: Review Cyberpunk 2020 2.0.2.0 as a standalone TTRPG system, tracing campaign identity, Roles, Lifepath, core resolution, economy, cyberware/Humanity, Friday Night Firefight, automatic fire, injury/medicine, Netrunning, vehicles/specialist systems, and Referee support.

delivery: current canonical reverse-engineering drill plus source-grounded subsystem analysis and practitioner lineage correction
notes: The study was deliberately rescaled after practitioner clarification that 1E–3E form one classic engine family. 3E was treated as the mature representative; 1E/2E remain lineage references rather than separately completed standalone cases. Source-specific judgments remain bounded to 3E until the 4E/5E redesigns are traced.
observations: Shadowrun 3E mechanically delivered professional-criminal identity through a dependency network of employers, contacts, legwork, black-market gear, lifestyle, cyberware, security, injury, repair, Karma, nuyen, and aftermath rather than through setting prose alone.

The classic engine reused one d6 success-count grammar across physical, magical, Matrix, and vehicle domains, but shared randomizer/resolution grammar did not imply shared procedure, state, or participation structure.
Renewable Dice Pools created strong short-horizon allocation when the same reserve had to serve offense, defense, self-protection, or specialist effect before a larger-cycle refresh.

Initiative was a structural action-economy multiplier: high speed produced more full actions and early wounds could reduce opponents' later actions, creating positive-feedback first-strike dominance and participation-cadence inequality.

Automatic fire preserved round-count, recoil, Power, Damage Level, Dodge difficulty, and ammunition while compressing multiple bullets into one attack event, so the major combat cadence problem came from action repetition rather than projectile-by-projectile resolution.

Essence functioned most cleanly as augmentation capacity and magic/healing compatibility rather than a universal morality meter; cyberware frequently created new interfaces while linking power to legality, access, biological cost, or support dependency.

Magic was a high-complexity but strongly integrated specialist superstructure: Force/Drain created endogenous counterpressure, Spell Defense produced teammate-facing decisions, and astral projection was the main parallel-play risk.

Matrix play combined excellent internal intrusion mechanics and strong shared-world outputs with weak shared-decision coupling; synchronized fictional time did not solve attention-time TBMD when exclusive decker operations chained together.

Rigging showed a healthier specialist architecture because privileged movement/control operated through shared vehicles where passengers remained active; drone networks still introduced actor-count inflation and remote-scouting isolation risks.
Preparation and legwork were strongest when they changed scenario topology by bypassing or transforming later obstacles rather than merely adding numeric bonuses.
Persistent wounds, vehicle/deck damage, hunted loot, compromised identities, favors, and repair/training needs created scenario-addressable aftermath even without a formal dynamic campaign generator.

Most major subsystems had defensible local purpose, yet aggregate complexity and gamemaster integration burden remained high, showing that locally justified complexity can still exceed a usable total human-operating budget.

delivery: current canonical reverse-engineering drill plus source-grounded subsystem analysis
notes: This event closes the standalone Shadowrun 4E case at Pass 12. No 3E→4E or 4E→5E delta is treated as completed here; edition-comparison claims remain deferred until the later comparison pass.
observations: Shadowrun 4E preserved the professional-specialist runner identity while replacing much of the classic engine with a unified fixed-TN hit-count grammar; specialist differentiation remained in world interfaces, capital, persistent state, and privileged access rather than requiring unrelated core resolvers.

The redesign repeatedly compressed common procedure without flattening consequence: automatic fire compressed multiple bullets into one attack while preserving recoil/armor/wound state, chase combat compressed continuous geometry into engagement ranges, Device Rating compressed unimportant networked electronics, and routine driving/shopping/discovery often required no roll.

The 400 BP chargen economy was expressive but mastery-sensitive because flat or packaged creation costs fed into progressively priced Karma advancement and separate nuyen, Essence, contact, and access economies, rewarding build-order and catalog knowledge.

Attribute dependency remained uneven; Agility and Logic carried broad skill coverage while Reaction and Intuition gained derived/high-cadence leverage, Magic acted as a dense specialist ceiling/infrastructure hub, and Edge combined resource capacity with spend potency.

Additional Initiative Passes remained an engine-wide power currency across augmentation, magic, adepts, VR, astral play, drones, sprites, and other actors. Repeated attacks could erode defense and inflict wound penalties that reduced Initiative, preserving positive-feedback tempo dominance and unequal participation cadence.

The wireless Matrix was a substantive integration success in AR because cameras, doors, communications, devices, accounts, datatrails, and shared overlays altered the same physical scenario the whole team was solving. Optimized VR nevertheless retained specialist decision isolation despite synchronized three-second turns, proving synchronization is not participation.

Vehicle rigging was a strong shared-platform model because the rigger controlled movement/position while passengers continued acting. Drone fleets exposed the opposite failure mode: cheap group commands reduced control bandwidth but did not reduce independently resolving actor cycles, so capital could purchase multiple three-pass action streams.

Capability repeatedly created dependency: wireless convenience created attack surface and evidence trails; augmentation consumed irreversible Essence and interacted with healing/legal access; sustaining, hot-sim, and jumped-in control exchanged performance for ongoing or neurological risk; contacts created favors; lifestyle created recurring economic pressure.

Preparation strongly changed problem topology through credentials, prepared Matrix exploits, physical jackpoints, astral reconnaissance, drone surveillance, contacts, and equipment acquisition; the strongest prep removed or replaced later live contests rather than merely adding bonuses.

GM operating burden fell locally through common grammar, grunt compression, Professional Rating, Device Rating, and routine-action omission, but remained high globally because more interoperable physical, Matrix, magical, vehicle, social, economic, legal, and reputational states had to be integrated in one shared operation.

Persistent aftermath remained a major strength through wounds, downtime, medical costs, burned identities, datatrails, astral signatures, favors, debts, Street Cred, Notoriety, Public Awareness, and institutional attention.

Standalone judgment: 4E is a strong mechanically substantive redesign with high purpose density; its deepest defects are action/actor multiplication, mastery-sensitive build economics, uneven dependency hubs, residual high-performance specialist isolation, and substantial cross-domain referee integration burden.
